about: C2a-01, pass 1: the arrows, each formed from the ledger and the within-case rooms and substantiated by c2_arrow_evidence.py (outputs c2_arrow_evidence-p1a.txt, -p1b.txt, -p1c.txt). Support codes are turned into quotes through cite.py by c2_build_model_p1.py; transitions name two coded turns in one thread by code, and the builder fills items, thread and interval from the store. Counts: rooms carrying both elements, holds, the observed share, and the permutation null (500 shuffles of labels within each room, seed 20261014).
sample_rule: sampled_against: rooms carrying both elements outside the arrow's subs, drawn by random.Random(20261014) in c2_arrow_evidence.py; holds when the connection statement holds in that room, fails when it does not

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first call for hands comes before the first build report
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the call themes and the build themes, first hour in each room, against a permutation null; 164 transitions in 70 rooms where a build report answers a call. Disconfirming: build reports only before any call, or calls with no build report after them.
arrows.mechanism: A call brings members to the canvas who then start or extend the mark and say how far it has come.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, build reports come only before any call, or calls are followed by no build report at all.
arrows.bound: Where a member has begun the mark before any call, the call follows the first build report and recruits to a mark already started.
arrows.counterexample_response: xenoblade_chronicles reports building at h25.0 and first calls at h33.6: a starter placed first and the call came to a mark already begun. 53 of the 190 rooms run this way. Response: a scope condition (the bound), not a withdrawal; the arrow keeps its order where the call opens the work, and the starter element (R01) carries the other route.
arrows.gloss: calls bring the hands that build

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first proposal or start of a mark comes before the first call for hands
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of proposing the room's mark and making a tribute alone, against the call themes; 59 transitions in 27 rooms where a call or pledge answers a proposal. Disconfirming: calls only before any proposal or start, or proposals that draw no call.
arrows.mechanism: A member who proposes or begins a mark gives the room something to answer, and calls for hands gather around it.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: Calls in a room come only before any proposal or start, or a proposal draws no call.
arrows.bound: Where the room calls for hands before anyone proposes what to make, the proposal answers the call instead.
arrows.counterexample_response: worldoftanks calls at h34.8 and its first proposal comes at h72.3, after a move: the call came first and the proposal later answered a loss. Response: a scope condition; 25 of the 89 rooms run this way.
arrows.gloss: a start gives the call something to gather around

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first build report comes before the first act of upkeep or defence
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the build themes against the repair and defence themes; 214 transitions in 85 rooms where upkeep answers a build report. Disconfirming: upkeep that starts before any build report, or a built mark never watched.
arrows.mechanism: Once a mark stands on a surface anyone can change, keeping it becomes the work: a finished part is something to lose.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, upkeep and defence come only before any build report, or a reported build is never watched or repaired.
arrows.bound: Where the room's mark was found already placed by others, or a rival attacked before the room reported building, upkeep comes first.
arrows.counterexample_response: 109 of the 291 rooms keep or defend before they report building. Response: a scope condition (the bound); the sampled rooms all hold, and the arrow keeps its order where the room builds its own mark.
arrows.gloss: a built mark becomes a mark to keep

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first act of upkeep or defence comes before the first border talk, truce or deal
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the repair and defence themes against the negotiated-order themes; 293 transitions in 129 rooms where talk with a neighbour answers upkeep or defence. Disconfirming: talk with neighbours only before any upkeep.
arrows.mechanism: Keeping a mark against erosion brings the room up against the neighbours whose pixels erode it, and the room turns to talk with them.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, border talk comes only before any upkeep or defence, or upkeep against a neighbour never turns to talk with it.
arrows.bound: On the late side, rooms that came to a full canvas talk with neighbours first, asking for space before they have a mark to keep (6 of 15 hold).
arrows.counterexample_response: 166 of the 401 rooms talk with neighbours before any upkeep, and the late side holds in only 6 of 15. Response: a scope condition (the bound), carried to the onset contrast.
arrows.gloss: keeping the mark brings the room to its neighbours

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first border talk, truce or deal comes before the first act of sparing a neighbour
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the negotiated-order themes against the restraint themes; 59 transitions in 31 rooms where sparing answers a settled border. Disconfirming: sparing only before any talk.
arrows.mechanism: A settled border gives members a line to keep, and they spare the neighbour's work by it and remind others of it.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, sparing comes only before any border talk, or a settled border is followed by no sparing.
arrows.bound: Sparing often comes first and tacit, before any talk; the arrow holds where restraint rests on a border already settled.
arrows.counterexample_response: edmontonoilers spares a neighbour at h13.3 and first talks of a border at h73.8; totallynotrobots spares at h71.0, talks at h71.7. Tacit restraint does not wait for an agreement (Live and let live). Response: a scope condition; the observed share only just beats the null's 95th percentile (0.671 against 0.658), so the arrow is thin.
arrows.gloss: a settled border is a line members keep

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first act of upkeep or defence comes before the first script, bot or extra account
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the repair and defence themes against the machine-hands themes; 117 transitions in 53 rooms where a script or spare account answers a defence. Disconfirming: scripts before any upkeep.
arrows.mechanism: Upkeep under attack outruns what one pixel per interval can hold, and members turn to scripts and spare accounts to keep up.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, scripts and spare accounts come only before any upkeep or defence, or a room under strain never reaches for them.
arrows.bound: Where a room scripted the building itself from the start, machine hands come before any upkeep.
arrows.counterexample_response: canucks runs a script at h29.3 before its first upkeep at h39.4. Response: a scope condition; 43 of 203 rooms run this way.

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first build report comes before the first marking of the finished work
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the build themes against the completion-ritual themes; 96 transitions in 47 rooms where 'we did it' or credit answers a build report. Disconfirming: celebration only before any build report.
arrows.mechanism: A mark reported done gives the room a finished thing to point at, and the room marks it together: announcement, credit, pride.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, celebration comes only before any build report, or a finished build is never marked.
arrows.bound: Where the room's first mark was found already made by others, the room celebrates the find before it builds anything itself.
arrows.counterexample_response: 100 of 282 rooms mark a work before their first build report. Response: a scope condition (the bound); the sampled rooms all hold.
arrows.gloss: a finished mark is marked together

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first marking of the finished work comes before the first record of what happened to it
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the completion-ritual themes against the collective-memory themes; 259 transitions in 108 rooms where a record or account answers a celebration. Disconfirming: records only before any celebration.
arrows.mechanism: Marking the work together turns members toward keeping it: they ask for the final image, the timelapse, the list of what changed.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, records come only before any celebration, or a celebrated work is never recorded.
arrows.bound: On the late side the record often comes first, a screenshot of a work found rather than built (8 of 15 hold).
arrows.counterexample_response: 64 of 289 rooms record before they celebrate; on the late side 7 of 15. Response: a scope condition carried to the onset contrast.
arrows.gloss: what is celebrated is kept on record

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first record of what happened comes before the first act of carrying the work on
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the collective-memory themes against the transition themes; 26 transitions in 13 rooms where carrying on answers a record. Disconfirming: plans to carry on only before any record.
arrows.mechanism: A record of the work gives the room something to carry: the image into the banner, the plan into the next canvas.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, plans to carry on come only before any record, or a recorded work is carried nowhere.
arrows.bound: Where a room planned its next canvas or its emblem while still building, carrying on comes before any record.
arrows.counterexample_response: texans carries the work on at h34.5 and records at h73.2. Response: a scope condition; 32 of 145 rooms run this way.
arrows.gloss: the record is what passes on

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first doubt about the room's numbers or room comes before the first move after a loss
arrows.grounding_note: Cited concepts of the collective-efficacy themes against relocating and weighing fight against move; 1 transition (paranatural). Disconfirming: moves with no doubt voiced before them.
arrows.mechanism: A room that judges it has too few hands to hold its spot stops fighting for it and moves.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: In a room, a move comes with no doubt voiced before it, or doubt about numbers is followed by no move and no surrender.
arrows.bound: Only 21 rooms carry both; where a room moves early by choice rather than after a loss, the move comes before any doubt.
arrows.counterexample_response: anarcho_capitalism moves at h9.0 and voices doubt at h32.9. Response: a scope condition; the arrow is thin on 21 rooms.
arrows.gloss: too few hands, so the room moves

arrows.connection: in a room carrying both, the first design talk comes before the first template (tested, not beaten: 0.556 against a null mean of 0.557)
arrows.grounding_note: The order between rooms is at chance, so the arrow rests on transitions: 82 in 36 rooms where a template answers design talk in one reply thread. Disconfirming: template revisions that answer no design talk.
arrows.mechanism: Design talk in a thread is settled by someone posting a template that fixes the agreed design pixel by pixel.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: Templates are revised in threads with no design talk before them, or design talk ends with no template.
arrows.bound: Inside reply threads only; across rooms the first template often comes before any design talk (texas: template at h5.9, design talk at h23.5), so it is not an order between rooms.
arrows.counterexample_response: texas and empiredidnothingwrong post templates long before design talk. Response: the arrow is restated as a transition inside threads, with base_rate_beaten false; its order claim is withdrawn.
arrows.gloss: a template settles a design argued in a thread

arrows.connection: a one-line pledge answers a call in the same thread (form-pass finding FP-01; never counted)
arrows.grounding_note: The form pass found 590 one-line replies in 337 rooms, 90.3% under a coded parent item, mostly calls, proposals and border posts; that figure describes the search and is not used as a count here. Instances read with mem.py after. Disconfirming: one-line pledges that answer nothing, or calls answered only at length.
arrows.mechanism: A call is answered at the lowest possible cost: one line that commits the member and asks for nothing back.
arrows.mechanism_fails_if: The one-line pledges in a room answer no call, or every answer to a call is long and conditional.
arrows.bound: Never counted: a form-pass finding travels on exemplars only.
arrows.gloss: the cheapest answer to a call
